findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced default encryption policy or customer-managed key.

findings.issue_category: no ACL or public access controls
findings.description: The bucket omits any acl setting and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults for blocking public access; combined with no bucket policy this is an unrestricted-exposure risk for archived report data.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this data bucket is not recorded to the audit_trail bucket, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrites or deletions (made trivially destructive by force_destroy = true) are unrecoverable and tampering cannot be detected.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without an enforced default encryption policy.
No logging block is configured for this financial data bucket, so there is no server access log record of who read or modified ledger exports.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true is set, meaning ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted by default, unlike the audit_trail bucket which uses a KMS CMK.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain internal hostnames, procedures, and occasionally credentials, are stored with no default server-side encryption configured.
No logging block is configured, so access to runbook content is not logged to the audit_trail bucket.
The audit log bucket has no bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so log delivery and retrieval may occur over plaintext HTTP.

force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows Terraform to delete all accumulated access logs (including versioned objects) in a single apply, undermining the integrity and non-repudiation of the audit record; no object lock or MFA delete is configured.
